# Stella Maynard

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- **Status:** poor  <sub>[v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052)</sub>
- **Origin:** Vancouver  <sub>[v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)</sub>
- **Role:** teacher  <sub>[v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022)</sub>
- **Titles:** rose-red girl  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Stella is a vivid, black-eyed girl who carried off the palm for beauty among the Second Year classes at Queen's Academy.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)_

## Personality

Stella is thoughtful, imaginative, and ambitious, possessing a heart full of aerial, rainbow-like wistful dreams and fancies. Though normally cheerful and calm, she occasionally experiences blue and discouraged moods where she questions the purpose of living. She deeply appreciates a cozy home, viewing living at Patty's Place as a jolly nest superior to boardinghouses.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010), [v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031), [v3 c38 P16](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0016)_

## History

Stella attended Queen's Academy in the Second Year class, where she formed an intimate circle of friends with Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant. After leaving Queen's, she worked as a schoolteacher for a time before deciding to attend Redmond College. She proposed renting Patty's Place to live with Anne, Priscilla, and her aunt, Aunt Jamesina, who kept house for them, later agreeing to include Philippa Gordon as a housemate. After completing her studies at Redmond with a good all-round showing at Convocation, she eventually moved to Vancouver, where she resumed teaching school.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c9 P6](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0006), [v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 c10 P47](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0047), [v3 c10 P59](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0059), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c37 P29](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0029), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Quotes

> I’m so glad we can keep Patty’s Place for another year. I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again.  <sub>[v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010)</sub>

> I’m blue and discouraged myself, throwing herself on the couch. Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?  <sub>[v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031)</sub>

> It does—but I am not jealous. I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina.  <sub>[v3 c38 P16](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0016)</sub>
